challenge.method: Rehashed both captured registry bodies, compared the candidate ID and every origin field, and checked the entire prior history against the accepted history prefix and appended predecessor. Recomputed the origin digest with an altered source locator. Compared both publisher files for a possible instrument swap and inspected Shield’s downstream notice and competition provisions.
challenge.results: Appending #altered changed the origin digest. The accepted history preserved the original entry and appended the exact unresolved disposition and reason. Substituting Perimeter would change the candidate ID, publisher key, title, version, path and origin digest. Shield’s competition language also addresses products the licensor or its affiliates provide using the software. Its Discontinued Products section uses “Licensor Line of Business” for that provision, while its Notices section addresses passing terms or their URL and supplied “Required Notice” lines to software recipients. These provisions serve distinct purposes and supply no additional identity or rights finding.

limitations: The two registry revisions share one record lineage. The publisher file establishes the edition label at the pinned revision. The live URL and byte equality across representations were outside this inspection.

Support extends only to recognition of the documentary binding. SPDX equivalence, license selection for a work, exercise of rights, downstream notice compliance and permission to redistribute license text each require separate evidence.
